title: 第7章 西边捡来的项西(7)

content_zh:
早上在泼泼们撕心裂肺的叫声中睁开眼睛，他伸了个懒腰，下床走到窗边，把窗帘拉开，用手指比了个手枪，对着对面阳台嘭嘭嘭嘭开了四枪，然后转身去洗漱。
刷牙的时候老妈的电话打了过来，程博衍接了电话，按下免提。
“起了吗？”老妈问。
“嗯，刷牙呢。”程博衍含着一口牙膏沫子说。
“开窗通通风，捂了一夜了，”老妈指点他，“今天空气质量优。”
“哦。”程博衍看了看外面，天有些阴，雪还下着，齁冷的，但他还是按老妈的指示这边的窗跟卧室的窗平行，一“你打豆浆吗？”老妈愣了愣，“这个豆浆机质量不行吧，怎么出这种声音，当心爆炸。”
“我还没买豆浆机，”程博衍吐掉牙膏沫，“这是对楼的鹦鹉。”
“太闹了……”老妈感叹了一句，接着提高了声音：“不是让你买豆浆机吗？说了都一个月了也没买？营养要均衡全面，早餐这么重要……”
“我今天下班就去买，”程博衍赶紧说，“下班就买，保证。”
“你要忙的话，我就买一个拿过去算了，昨天你大姨给拿了些鲜的铁皮石斛，正好一块儿拿过去给你。”老妈说。
“我要那个干吗？”程博衍叹了口气。
“增强免疫力，你这整天忙着工作，生活没个规律，晚睡早起的，这个每天吃点儿对身体好……”
“知道了，”程博衍打断老妈的话，家里有个营养师的感觉挺不好形容的，“我今天下了班过去拿吧，你别跑了。”
“是怕我过去看到你过得乱七八糟吧。”老妈笑了笑。
其实程博衍觉得自己现在这情况，已经算是单身男人当中相当少见的了。
拜老妈所赐的各种强迫症让他的房间干净整洁，纤尘不染，进门消毒液擦手，出门的衣服单独放在一个柜子里，吃饭不到万不得已不叫外卖，一般情况下都吃按老妈的各种营养菜谱用自己堪比毒师的手艺做出来的恐怖食物……
程博衍吃完早餐出了门，早餐是各种豆子和薏米煮的一锅杂豆粥，营养是很好，味道就……用他的手艺煮出来的实在是有些回味悠长。
程博衍今天上午在住院部，下午出门诊，时间安排得挺紧张。
路过厕所的时候，碰上了放射科的李大夫，打了个招呼他就被李大夫叫住了：“小程，昨天不是说有骨折的病人过来拍片子吗？怎么没来啊？”
“嗯？”程博衍愣了，“没来？伤得挺重的，我还估计着要住院呢。”

“是啊，没来，后来过来的三个都不是骨折的。”李大夫说。
还真是碰瓷的？
程博衍突然有些郁闷，现在碰瓷的真是一个比一个敬业，伤了就赶紧趁机上街找苦主去，来医院之前不定讹了几个了，最后还能做到过医院而不入，不，过医院而不治……
他想起了那个展宏图迷茫而单纯的眼神，还有那声透着乖巧的“哥”，演技不错啊！
还展宏图呢，大展碰瓷之宏图吧！
郁闷是挺郁闷，不过换了衣服去查房的时候，程博衍还是忍不住琢磨了一下这事，确切地说是展宏图的那个伤。
碰瓷这职业不知道工作周期是多少天，这种单纯腓骨骨折，恢复起来不难，但总这么拖着条腿在街上又是蹦又是跳的，还要撞车，时间长了若骨头移位严重，就不好说了。
“程大夫早啊。”旁边有人叫了他一声。
程博衍转过头，看到病房里一个小姑娘正靠在床头跟他打招呼，这小姑娘十七岁，住进来一个星期了。
“早啊，”他笑了笑，走了进去，“今天感觉怎么样？”
“还是疼，”小姑娘皱皱眉，指着自己的大腿，“就靠近膝盖那边，是骨癌吗？”
“这个得明天做了活检才能最后确定，”程博衍看着她，“好好休息，你妈妈几点过来？”
“已经过来了，去给我买杂志了。”小姑娘笑着说，又垂下眼皮，“程大夫。”
“嗯？”程博衍看了看她床头放着的一个龙猫。
“就是骨癌吧，”小姑娘抬起头，拿着手机晃了晃，“我查了，很像啊。”
程博衍心里抽了一下，弯下腰拿过她的手机放到旁边床头柜上，笑着说：“自己能查明白还要医生干吗，好好休息，今天梁主任会来跟你谈话，他很有经验，放心。”

content_en:
When he opened his eyes in the morning to the heart-rending screams of the thugs, he stretched out, got out of bed and walked to the window, opened the curtains, gestured with a pistol with his finger, fired four shots at the opposite balcony, and then turned around to wash up.
While I was brushing my teeth, my mother's phone called. Cheng Boyan answered the phone and pressed the speaker phone.
"Are you up?" Mom asked.
"Well, I'm brushing my teeth." Cheng Boyan said with a mouthful of toothpaste foam.
"Open the windows to ventilate the air. I've been covering it up all night," his mother instructed him. "The air quality is excellent today."
"Oh." Cheng Boyan looked outside. The sky was a little overcast, the snow was still falling, and it was cold, but he still followed his mother's instructions. The window here was parallel to the window of the bedroom. "Are you making soy milk?" His mother was stunned. "The quality of this soy milk machine is not good. Why does it make such a sound? Be careful of explosion."
"I haven't bought a soymilk machine yet," Cheng Boyan spat out the toothpaste foam, "This is the parrot on the opposite floor."
"It's too noisy..." Mom sighed, and then raised her voice: "Didn't I ask you to buy a soymilk machine? You haven't bought it even after a month? Nutrition must be balanced and comprehensive, and breakfast is so important..."
"I'll buy it after get off work today," Cheng Boyan said quickly, "I'll buy it after get off work, I promise."
"If you're busy, I'll just buy one and take it over. Yesterday, your aunt brought some fresh dendrobium, so I'll just give it to you together." Mom said.
"Why do I want that?" Cheng Boyan sighed.
"Enhance your immunity. You have been busy working all day and have no routine. You go to bed late and get up early. Eating something of this every day is good for your health..."
"I know," Cheng Boyan interrupted his mother. The feeling of having a nutritionist at home was indescribable. "I'll go get it after work today. Don't run away."
"I'm afraid I'll see you living in a mess." Mom smiled.
In fact, Cheng Boyan feels that his current situation is quite rare among single men.
Thanks to the various obsessive-compulsive disorders given by his mother, his room is clean and tidy, spotless, he wipes his hands with disinfectant when he comes in, puts his clothes in a separate cupboard when he goes out, doesn't order takeout when he doesn't have enough meals, and usually eats horrible food made according to his mother's various nutritional recipes with his craftsmanship comparable to a poison master...
Cheng Boyan went out after breakfast. Breakfast was a pot of miscellaneous bean porridge cooked with various beans and barley. It was very nutritious and tasted...it was cooked with his craftsmanship and had a long aftertaste.
Cheng Boyan was in the inpatient department this morning and went out to the outpatient department in the afternoon. The schedule was quite tight.
When passing by the toilet, he met Dr. Li from the radiology department. He said hello and was stopped by Dr. Li: "Xiao Cheng, didn't you say yesterday that patients with fractures came to take X-rays? Why didn't they come?"
"Huh?" Cheng Boyan was stunned, "Not here? The injury is quite serious. I think he will be hospitalized."
"Yes, I didn't come. None of the three who came later had fractures." Doctor Li said.
Is it really a scam?
Cheng Boyan suddenly felt a little depressed. Nowadays, everyone who touches porcelain is more dedicated than the other. When he is injured, he quickly takes the opportunity to go to the street to find the victim. He may have blackmailed a few people before coming to the hospital. In the end, he was able to pass the hospital without being admitted. No, he passed the hospital without being treated...
He thought of Zhan Hongtu's confused and innocent eyes, and his well-behaved "Brother". What an excellent acting skill!
Let’s show off our grand plans, let’s show off our grand plans!
It was quite depressing, but when he changed his clothes and went to check the ward, Cheng Boyan couldn't help but think about it, specifically the injury on Zhan Hongtu.
I don’t know how many days the working cycle of this profession is. It is not difficult to recover from such a simple fibula fracture, but I am always dragging my leg on the street, jumping and jumping, and crashing. After a long time, if the bone is seriously displaced, it will be difficult to say.
"Good morning, Doctor Cheng." Someone called him next to him.
Cheng BoyanzhuanLooking over his shoulder, he saw a little girl in the ward leaning on the bedside to greet him. The girl was seventeen years old and had been here for a week.
"Morning," he smiled and walked in, "How are you feeling today?"
"It still hurts," the little girl frowned, pointing to her thigh, "it's near the knee. Is it bone cancer?"
"This will have to be confirmed through a biopsy tomorrow," Cheng Boyan looked at her, "Have a good rest. When will your mother come over?"
"I'm already here, going to buy me a magazine." The little girl said with a smile, and then lowered her eyelids, "Doctor Cheng."
"Huh?" Cheng Boyan looked at a chinchilla on her bedside.
"It must be bone cancer." The little girl raised her head and waved her cell phone. "I checked, and it looks very similar."
Cheng Boyan's heart twitched, and he bent down to take her mobile phone and put it on the bedside table next to him. He said with a smile: "You can figure out why you need a doctor. Have a good rest. Director Liang will come to talk to you today. He is very experienced. Don't worry."
